entries.en:
Are you familiar with forklifts?
In this feature, we will explore the appeal of these machines, which play such an important role at ports and warehouses.
Unlike ordinary cars, forklifts steer with their rear wheels, making them far more maneuverable in tight spaces.
The forks mounted at the front can also lift cargo such as containers.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k122; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Did you know that warehouses with functions beyond simply storing cargo are now being developed and sold?
This time, we introduce a warehouse that doubles as a nuclear shelter. Even ten consecutive direct hits from nuclear missiles will neither destroy nor contaminate it. Special purification and air-conditioning equipment keeps the air inside clean, while Omoto Trading's Ultra Super Solar system supplies power, making it practically a perpetual-motion machine.

Unfortunately, you must provide your own food, but with so much space, growing vegetables inside the warehouse could be an option.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k208; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Did you know there are warehouses that can move on caterpillar tracks?
They let you move the cargo together with the entire warehouse.

They are already in use in a certain country where most of the land has become desert. The sight of refrigerated and frozen-storage warehouses crossing the desert like caravans of old is truly impressive.
More wharves are reportedly adopting them, too, because moving the entire warehouse during a disaster can prevent further damage.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k210; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Believe it or not, there are warehouses that can fly using jet propulsion.
They need no runway, since they can move like aircraft capable of vertical flight.
Another feature is that Omoto Trading's Ultra Super Solar system powers them, eliminating worries about fuel costs.

With the warehouse itself providing transportation, entire warehouses can now be shipped around.

They also offer a revolutionary evacuation method during earthquakes and other disasters: retreating into the unaffected sky. Adoption has therefore begun at public facilities as well as businesses.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k212; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
Some warehouses can themselves become ships.

Equipped with propulsion, they can take cargo out to sea and transport it as an entire warehouse, without transferring anything aboard a ship.
Many of you have probably seen the recent commercial in which numerous warehouses line up in the middle of the Pacific to form the company's logo. This is the product shown there.
entries.notes: English draft imported from audited private workspace, translate-en-0079.json:p0/k214; human editorial and runtime review pending.

entries.en:
There is a warehouse equipped with every kind of function.
It can serve as a nuclear shelter, travel on caterpillar tracks, fly through the sky with jets, and even become a ship.
Its price is on an entirely different scale from the others, but it is, so to speak, the ultimate warehouse.

You might think it could be used for military purposes, but apparently the company's peace-loving president strictly forbids that.
Do you remember the incident about six months ago when a certain country ruled by a tyrant was reduced to scorched earth overnight?
Rumors circulating with an air of credibility say this happened because secretly buying one of these warehouses and trying to misuse it incurred the president's wrath.
Of course, all uninvolved civilians were moved to other countries first. What a splendid deed.
